# Welcome to the Post Office Horizon IT Inquiry website This is an independent public statutory Inquiry established to gather a clear account of the implementation and failings of the Horizon IT system at the Post Office over its lifetime. ## Inquiry publishes Volume 1 of Final Report  Sir Wyn Williams has published the first volume of his final report, which focuses on the human impact of the Horizon scandal and redress (compensation).   In this report, Sir Wyn details the scale of the suffering endured by those affected by the Horizon scandal.    He also makes urgent recommendations to be taken to ensure ‘full and fair’ compensation is delivered to sub-postmasters affected by the Horizon scandal.   * Read the report in English * Read our news story about the report * Watch Sir Wyn's address after publishing the report * Read a summary of the report * Read background and statistics about the Inquiry * Read the recommendations in Welsh -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Horizon redress schemes: independent reports on scheme progress - GOV.UK (https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/horizon-redress-schemes-independent-reports-on-scheme-progress) 【turn426721search2】 [wordlim: 200] Published: 10 months ago; Crawled: yesterday; # Horizon redress schemes: independent reports on scheme progress Reports on how redress in the Group Litigation Order (GLO) scheme, the Horizon Convictions Redress Scheme (HCRS) and the Horizon Shortfall Scheme Appeals (HSSA) process are progressing. This page contains independent reports on redress for postmasters impacted by the Post Office Horizon Scandal. Written by Dentons, these reports detail the progress of claims in the Group Litigation Order (GLO (Group Litigation Order)) Compensation Scheme, the Horizon Convictions Redress Scheme and the Horizon Shortfall Scheme Appeals process. Reports published prior to 30 September 2025 cover the GLO (Group Litigation Order) Compensation Scheme only. Information about amounts paid out for all Horizon schemes is available separately on GOV.UK. From: Department for Business and Trade Published: 9 October 2025 Last updated: 19 March 2026 1. 19 March 2026 'Post Office Horizon IT Inquiry: update on restorative justice programme' was added to this collection. 2. 31 October 2025 'Post Office Horizon IT Inquiry: joint statement on restorative justice' added to collection. 3. 9 October 2025 First published. ## Contents 1. Report responses 2. Statements Chaired by Sir Wyn Williams, a former High Court judge, the inquiry aims to examine the failures of the Horizon IT system, which led to the wrongful suspension, termination, and prosecution of sub-postmasters over more than 2 decades. More information about the inquiry is available on the Post Office Horizon IT Inquiry website ### Report responses * Government response to the Post Office Horizon IT Inquiry report (volume 1) * 12 February 2026 * Policy paper * Response to Post Office Horizon IT inquiry interim report: compensation * 26 October 2023 * Correspondence ### Statements * Post Office Horizon IT Inquiry: update on restorative justice programme * 19 March 2026 * Policy paper * Post Office Horizon IT Inquiry: joint statement on restorative justice * 31 October 2025 * Policy paper * Post Office Horizon IT Inquiry: statement on full and fair financial redress * 9 October 2025 * Correspondence -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Compensation Payments: Deliver recommendations from Volume 1 of the Post Office Horizon IT Inquiry's final report (https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/69283abea245b0985f0341b7/Budget_2025_Policy_Costings.pdf) 【turn426721search12】 [wordlim: 200] Published: 11 months ago; Compensation Payments: Deliver recommendations from Volume 1 of the Post Office Horizon IT Inquiry's final report ## Measure description This measure enables implementation of the recommendations in the Post Office Horizon IT Inquiry Report (Volume 1). Redress payments are provided by the Department for Business and Trade and Post Office Limited under four current schemes: Horizon Shortfall Scheme (HSS); Horizon Shortfall Scheme Appeals (HSSA); Group Litigation Order (GLO) Scheme; and Horizon Convictions Redress Scheme (HCRS), and a new scheme is being established for family members of Horizon Scandal victims. The Overturned Convictions scheme is now closed. This measure was announced on 9 October 2025, and implementation is ongoing. ## The cost base The cost base for this measure includes estimates of cost impacts of changes to existing Post Office Horizon scandal redress schemes delivered by Post Office Limited and the Department for Business and Trade. It also includes initial estimates of the number of family members of Horizon Scandal victims who are expected to be eligible to claim compensation through a new redress scheme that is being established by the Department for Business and Trade. ## Costing The costing is based on expected impacts of changes to the approach taken in existing redress schemes and initial estimates of the expected number of family members who may be eligible and come forward to claim under the new scheme, expected levels of redress payments and the timing of redress payments. This costing assumes no behavioural impacts. ## Exchequer impact (£m)

## Areas of uncertainty The main uncertainties in this costing relate to the final design of the new family members scheme, number of claimants that come forward, how quickly claims progress and the scale of awards made. 88 -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Post Office Inquiry to publish Volume 1 of its final report, covering compensation and human impact | Post Office Horizon IT Inquiry (https://www.postofficehorizoninquiry.org.uk/news/post-office-inquiry-publish-volume-1-its-final-report-covering-compensation-and-human-impact) 【turn426721search5】 [wordlim: 200] Published: 1.5 years ago; Crawled: today; # Post Office Inquiry to publish Volume 1 of its final report, covering compensation and human impact 15 May 2025 Inquiry Chair Sir Wyn Williams has announced today (15/05/25) that he intends to publish the first part of his final report this summer. This volume will focus on redress (compensation) and the human impact of the scandal. Sir Wyn Williams said: “Throughout my investigations, I have heard how people have faced unimaginable hardship due to the impacts of the Horizon scandal, from wrongful convictions and financial ruin to broken relationships and severe emotional distress. I have also held several compensation hearings, which have stressed the urgency for people to receive redress that is full, fair and prompt. “I have always been of the view that those who have been affected by the Horizon scandal should be at the heart of the Inquiry’s work. So, it seems fitting that my conclusions on the suffering endured by so many, as well as the issue of redress, should be at the forefront of my report and published as soon as feasibly possible.” The report will be published on the Inquiry website and laid in Parliament in line with the Inquiry’s Terms of Reference. Under Rule 13 of the Inquiry Rules 2006, the Inquiry has issued warning letters to those criticised in the report, allowing them a reasonable opportunity to respond. More information about the date of publication will follow in due course.   Notes to editors: * Information about publication date will be shared in due course. * This report will consider the human impact of the scandal and compensation (redress).   * Findings for the remaining phases, as well as overall recommendations, will follow in a final report, to be published in due course. * Alongside the publication of Volume 1 of the final report, the Inquiry is also working to publish all the evidence that has been shown in hearings and mentioned in witness statements. Moving forward, the Inquiry will no longer be able to consider individual requests to publish specific documents. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Volume 1 — Searchable transcripts of the Post Office Horizon IT Inquiry hearings documentation (https://postofficeinquiry.dracos.co.uk/report/volume-1/) 【turn426721search6】 [wordlim: 200] Published: 1.3 years ago; Crawled: 5 months ago; # Volume 1 Volume 1 was published on 8th July 2025. * 1. In respect of those 425 claims, offers in settlement had been made in 407 cases. 269 claimants had accepted their offers, and 265 claimants had actually been paid. There remained 67 claims in which full claims had not been made. 4.231. By 7 April 2025 there were further changes. 446 claims had been received. 432 offers had been made of which 287 had been accepted and 282 claimants had been paid.¹⁴ 4.232. As of 30 April 2025, 450 claims had been submitted, and 445 offers had been made. 304 offers had been accepted, and 294 claimants had been paid.¹⁵ 4.233. In summary, by 30 April 2025 there were 42 claimants who had not submitted a particularised claim i.e. just under 9% of those entitled to claim. By the same date offers had been made to 445 claimants, i.e. just over 99% of the claimants who had made a claim had received offers. There were 188 unresolved claims, i.e. the claims of about 38% of those entitled to claim were unresolved. It is reasonable to infer that most of those claims are at various stages of assessment. It is difficult to imagine that there are a substantial number of claimants who are waiting to opt for, or accept a Fixed Sum Offer, given that the scheme has now been open for more than two years, and the Fixed Sum Offer has been available since January 2024. 4.234. I understand from Mr Creswell's fourth witness statement that there have been no further referrals to the panel since he gave oral evidence on 6 November 2024.¹⁶ I understand that 10 more claims have been referred to the panel since 31 March 2025, bringing the total number of referrals to 12 in total. One of the claims which had been referred to the panel on a non-binding basis has now been considered further by the panel and it has issued a binding determination. Following that binding determination a review was sought; the review has been undertaken by Sir Ross who has issued his decision.¹⁷ 4.235. By 30 April 2025, the Department had paid the total sum of £160m to claimants.¹⁸ This figure includes all full and final awards and interim payments. I did not consider it necessary to obtain a further witness statement on this point. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Post Office Horizon scandal: Justice for sub-postmasters (https://publications.parliament.uk/pa/cm5901/cmselect/cmbeis/1598/report.html) 【turn426721search7】 [wordlim: 200] Published: 7 months ago; Crawled: yesterday; # Post Office Horizon scandal: Justice for sub-postmasters This is a House of Commons committee report, with recommendations to government. The Government has two months to respond. ## Sixteenth Report of Session 2024–26 Author: Business and Trade Committee Date Published: Friday 13 March 2026 ## Summary One year on from the Committee’s last report on the Post Office Horizon scandal, progress has been made delivering redress for victims. But it is not job done. Over 11,300 claimants have now received payments and £1.44 billion has been distributed. But thousands of sub-postmasters are still waiting for the full and fair redress they are owed. Serious structural failings persist. Many victims still face unacceptable delays, inadequate offers, and administrative processes that re-traumatise those who have already been wronged. Meanwhile, the technology company Fujitsu, which played a central role in the scandal, has contributed nothing to the bill for redress, and is still growing its public sector revenues. * The continued administration of the Horizon Shortfall Scheme (HSS) by Post Office Ltd.^{6} * Persistent delays in issuing and paying both fixed-sum and fully-assessed HSS offers. There are no binding statutory or contractual timeframes in place, contrary to our previous recommendations, and Post Office Ltd continues to fall far behind its own targets.^{7} Fixed-sum offers currently take an average of 143 days to issue, more than four and a half times the intended 30-day target.^{8} Fully-assessed cases take an average of 450 days; two and a half times the 180 day target.^{9} * The continued absence of funded legal advice for claimants navigating the HSS.^{10} * Persistent under-valuation of fully-assessed HSS offers.^{11} * Ongoing difficulties in identifying sub-postmasters potentially eligible to have their convictions quashed under the Post Office (Horizon System) Offences Act 2024.^{12} 5. We therefore continued our scrutiny of the delivery of redress and justice for the sub-postmasters in an evidence session on 6 January 2026. We heard from a wide range of witnesses, including: claimants who had to fight to have their convictions quashed under the Post Office Horizon System Offences Act 2024; claimants’ lawyers; Fujitsu; Post Office Ltd; the Criminal Cases Review Commission (CCRC); and Government Ministers from the Ministry of Justice (MoJ) and the Department for Business and Trade (DBT). We identified outstanding issues with the operation of redress schemes and the Post Office (Horizon System) Offences Act 2024. These include: * access to fast and fair redress across the schemes; * the administration of the Horizon Shortfall Scheme (HSS); * the values of offers made under the HSS; * the Ministry of Justice (MoJ)’s processes for quashing Horizon-related convictions; * Fujitsu’s role in redress payments; and * the identification of sub-postmasters with potentially unsafe convictions as a result of pre-Horizon IT software. ## 2 Overview of Redress Schemes 6. Progress has been made across all the redress schemes since our last report, in both redress offers and payment rates, despite a continuing increase in the number of claims. Over 11,300 claimants had received redress payments by January 2026, compared to 4,300 a year earlier.^{13} As of 31 January 2026, approximately £1.44 billion has been paid out.^{14} Table 1 below summarises this progress between January 2025 and January 2026. A more detailed breakdown of progress can be found in Table 2 in Annex 1. Table 1: Progress of redress offers and payments per scheme, January 2025 and January 2026 Date | Scheme | Total Claims received | Total Offers made | % of Claims without offers | Total Offers accepted | % of accepted Offers awaiting payment | Total Claims Paid | Total Claims Paid (%) January 2025 | HSS (original deadline–up to March 2021) | 2,417 | 2,417 | 0% | 2,094 | 0.2% | 2,090 | 87% HSS (late claims) | 4,665 | 1,802 | 61% | 1,306 | 3.5% | 1,260 | 27% ## 3 Horizon Shortfall Scheme (HSS) ### Administration of the Horizon Shortfall Scheme 20. The Horizon Shortfall Scheme (HSS) is open to sub-postmasters who had to cover financial shortfalls arising from errors in the Horizon IT system, but who were neither convicted nor involved in the High Court litigation against Post Office Ltd.^{39} Under the scheme, eligible individuals may opt to accept a fixed-sum payment of £75,000 or pursue an individually-assessed award based on evidence of their financial and other losses.^{40} The HSS is administered by Post Office Ltd and applications for the scheme closed on 31 January 2026.^{41} Appeals against HSS awards are handled through the Horizon Shortfall Scheme Appeals (HSSA), which is run by the Department for Business and Trade (DBT), and has been open for applications since April 2025.^{42} 21. Both the issuing of fixed-sum offers and the subsequent payment process in the HSS remain slower than acceptable. On average, Post Office Ltd takes 143 calendar days to issue the £75,000 fixed-sum redress offer, which is more than four and a half times longer than their 30-day target.^{43} Payment is then made, on average, eight business days after the claimant accepts the offer.^{44} However, Post Office Ltd has improved its efficiency in administering the fixed-sum £75,000 redress. In 2025, Post Office Ltd processed and paid 8,000 fixed-sum claims, up from 1,000 in 2024.^{45} As a result, the proportion of outstanding HSS fixed-sum claims fell from 55% at the end of 2024 to 18% at the end of 2025.^{46} Post Office Ltd told the Committee that 80% of all remaining HSS cases relate to the fixed-sum offer, and that it expects to have completed these simpler cases by summer 2026.^{47} This is welcome. 22. Despite progress on handling fixed-sum claims, significant issues remain in the handling of more complex fully-assessed cases under the HSS. Post Office Ltd told us that it anticipates that around 500 of the remaining 2,498 unpaid claims (as of 19 December 2025) require full assessment.^{48} Post Office Ltd told us that these will not be completed until the end of 2026 or early 2027. More than 11,300 claimants have received payments with £1.44 billion distributed.  * Read the report (HTML) * Read the report (PDF) * Inquiry information * Business and Trade Committee But thousands of sub‑postmasters are still waiting for the redress they are owed, and in a report today the Committee says “serious structural failings persist” in the redress system. Many victims still face unacceptable delays, inadequate offers, and administrative processes that “re‑traumatise” those who have already been seriously wronged. Fujitsu, with a central role in one of the greatest miscarriages of justice in British history, has contributed nothing to the bill for redress and is still expanding its public sector revenues. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Post Office Corporate (https://corporate.postoffice.co.uk/horizon-scandal-pages/horizon-shortfall-scheme-information-and-data) 【turn426721search9】 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: last month; * # Horizon Shortfall Scheme: information and data Post Office is taking determined action to pay full and fair final financial redress for victims of the Horizon Scandal. The Horizon Shortfall Scheme (HSS) is for current and former postmasters who believe they experienced shortfalls related to previous versions of the Horizon system.  The scheme closed to new applications on 31 January 2026. Applications which were received before the closing date are being progressed.  More information is available on the scheme website, including frequently asked questions and details of the ongoing support available for applicants.  This page provides background information and progress data on payments that have been made. Total payments of more than £1,055m have been made through the Scheme as at 31 August 2026. You can access the latest redress figures here and at the bottom of this page. We will continue to update this page monthly.  ### Background information  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Horizon redress schemes: progress reports for 2025 - GOV.UK (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/horizon-redress-schemes-progress-reports-for-2025) 【turn426721search10】 [wordlim: 200] Published: 10 months ago; Crawled: today; # Horizon redress schemes: progress reports for 2025 Reports on how redress in the Group Litigation Order (GLO) Scheme, the Horizon Convictions Redress Scheme (HCRS) and the Horizon Shortfall Scheme Appeals (HSSA) process are progressing. ## Updates to this page From: Department for Business and Trade and Post Office Published: 31 December 2025 Last updated: 11 March 2026 1. 11 March 2026 The 'December 2025: report on GLO, HCRS and HSSA progress' has been added to the page. 2. 31 December 2025 First published. ## Documents ### December 2025: report on GLO, HCRS and HSSA progress HTML ### September 2025: report on GLO, HCRS, and HSSA progress HTML ### June 2025: report on GLO Compensation Scheme progress HTML ### April 2025: report on GLO Compensation Scheme progress HTML ### January 2025: report on GLO Compensation Scheme progress HTML ## Details This page contains independent reports on redress for postmasters impacted by the Post Office Horizon Scandal. Information about amounts paid out for all Horizon schemes is available separately on GOV.UK. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Written questions and answers - Written questions, answers and statements - UK Parliament (https://questions-statements.parliament.uk/written-questions/detail/2026-03-18/HL15737) 【turn426721search11】 [wordlim: 200] Published: 7 months ago; Crawled: yesterday; ### Question Lord Wigley Plaid Cymru Life peer Lords To ask His Majesty's Government what is their latest estimate of the total cost of the compensation claims against the Post Office for wrongful action against sub-postmasters. ### Answer Baroness Lloyd of Effra Labour Life peer Lords ### Answered on 26 March 2026 As of 27 February 2026, approximately £1.475 billion has been paid to over 11,500 claimants across the Horizon redress schemes. The Department publishes monthly reports updating this figure. Total spend to date and future commitments for victims of the Horizon scandal are estimated at £2.3 billion. In addition, over £1.6 million has been paid to claimants under the Capture redress scheme since its launch on 29 October 2025 The Government has not set a cap on either the Horizon or Capture redress schemes. The final cost will depend on how many victims come forward and the specific circumstances of their claims. ### Answered by Department for Business and Trade -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Daily Report of Written Answers and Written Statements (https://qna.files.parliament.uk/qnadailyreports/Written-Questions-Answers-Statements-Daily-Report-Lords-2026-03-26.pdf) 【turn426721search14】 [wordlim: 200] Published: 7 months ago; 6 Thursday 26 March 2026 Written Answers Written Answers BUSINESS AND TRADE ■ **Horizon IT system: Compensation** [HL15737] **Lord Wigley:** To ask His Majesty's Government what is their latest estimate of the total cost of the compensation claims against the Post Office for wrongful action against sub-postmasters. **Baroness Lloyd of Effra:** As of 27 February 2026, approximately £1.475 billion has been paid to over 11,500 claimants across the Horizon redress schemes.
